A field service management app helps businesses that send technicians to customer sites manage their work. It covers work orders, scheduling, inspections, job reports and customer communication in one place.

The office plans and assigns jobs, technicians see what they need on their phone, and managers can see where every job stands, without chasing updates across spreadsheets, group chats and paper job sheets. With Noloco, you build that app around your own process, on your own data.

With Noloco you build your own work order app on your own data, with a mobile view for technicians, inspection checklists, recurring maintenance visits and a portal where customers request work and follow its status.
The essentials are work orders with status, priority, customer and site; scheduling and dispatch, so you can see who is working where; and a mobile app technicians actually use on site.

Most teams also need inspection forms and checklists with photos, recurring maintenance visits, role-based permissions for technicians, office staff and managers, and a customer portal for job requests and status updates. With Noloco, all of these live in one app that you shape around your own process.
Can my technicians use it on their phones?

You can, and many field service teams start that way. A work order tracking spreadsheet works while a few people update it from the office. It gets harder once technicians need to update jobs from site, two people edit the same row, or customers keep calling to ask where their job is.

With Noloco you don't start over: import the spreadsheet from Excel or Google Sheets, and it becomes a work order app with a mobile view for technicians, permissions for each role, and workflows that keep the office and your customers up to date.

Tell Nola how your jobs, technicians and customers fit together and it sets up the tables, pages and workflows. After that, changes are yours to make: add a field to your work orders, change an inspection checklist, or set up a workflow that tells the office when a job is complete. No code, and no developer.

What they have in common is work that happens at customer sites: jobs to schedule, technicians to send out, checklists to complete and reports to deliver. Because each team builds its app around its own process, the same platform fits very different kinds of field work.
